items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: Right. Well at NBC they got Toscannini.

ctx.x: They had some fairly well known classical people head up those orchestras, didn’t they?

Right. Well at NBC they got Toscannini. At CBS Paul Lavalle had the City Services Concert band, and at ABC very often we had Arthur Fiedler. And we had others, because they did the Metropolitan Opera auditions on the air, and they did “Music for a Summer Night” and “Voice of Firestone,” and they would very often have guest conductors come in for those things.
Was most of the music you recorded in those orchestra situations, was it going on tape for use later? Or was it live?

items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: There was a tremendous amount of work. At that time, when I first started subbing up there, I think each of the networks had 95 musicians on staff. Each had 95 men on staff.

That’s right. They all had at least 95 men on staff, and then they would augment the orchestra, if they needed more. At that same time you had staff orchestras in Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Chicago, Cleveland. You had them all over at each of the networks. A lot of work.
